You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily｜U.S.-Iran Temporary Ceasefire Expires, Oil Surges; 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Since 2007; Microsoft and Meta Drag Tech Lower (August 18, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot Topics
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Long-end Treasury sell-off intensifies; 30-year yield hits highest level since 2007
The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield rose nearly 6 basis points on Monday to 5.31%, the highest since 2007; the 10-year yield stood around 4.72%.
Last week’s 30-year new-issue auction cleared at 5.216%, the highest since 2001.
Market concerns center on nearly $2 trillion in annual fiscal deficits continuously boosting supply, combined with inflation remaining above target and rising corporate issuance linked to AI infrastructure.
Market impact : The rapid rise in long-end yields increases financing costs and puts pressure on high-valuation growth stocks, while reinforcing cautious pricing of the Fed’s policy path.
International Commodities
U.S.-Iran temporary ceasefire expires; Hormuz risks re-escalate
The temporary ceasefire agreement signed by the U.S. and Iran in June expired on Monday; President Trump stated he would not extend it.
A senior Iranian official said that if diplomatic efforts fail to reach a permanent arrangement, Iran will shift to a “full-scale offensive” military posture and prepare to respond to the U.S. naval blockade.
The main disagreement remains control of the Strait of Hormuz; Brent crude closed up more than $2 to $90.87 per barrel on Monday, while average U.S. gasoline prices rose above $4 per gallon.
Market impact : Geopolitical risk premium has quickly returned, oil prices have risen significantly, rekindling inflation concerns and increasing short-term volatility in energy markets.
Macroeconomic Policy
Foreign holdings of U.S. Treasuries decline; U.S. may require allies to choose between U.S. and China AI frameworks
Overseas investors’ holdings of U.S. Treasuries fell by $72.1 billion in June, with both Japan and China reducing their positions.
According to a U.S. State Department internal draft letter seen by Reuters, the U.S. is preparing to require relevant countries to choose between U.S.- or China-led AI frameworks; simultaneous participation in Chinese initiatives could lead to exclusion from the U.S. “Pax Silica” alliance.
Anthropic’s annualized revenue run-rate has surpassed $65 billion, accelerating commercialization.
Market impact : Concerns over Treasury supply, combined with geopolitical tensions and the politicization of AI, increase market uncertainty. AI commercialization progress draws attention, but policy divergence risks are rising.
II. Market Recap
Commodities FX Performance
Spot Gold : approx. $4,432 per ounce, +0.37%
Spot Silver : approx. $66.46 per ounce, +1.05%
WTI Crude : approx. $84 per barrel, +0.35%
Brent Crude : approx. $87.12 per barrel, +0.29%
U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) : approx. 99.54, -0.02%
Driver analysis : The expiration of the U.S.-Iran temporary ceasefire and unresolved disagreements have re-escalated Hormuz risks, driving a notable rise in oil prices. Gold and silver found support amid geopolitical safe-haven demand and a softer dollar. The asset linkage is clear: geopolitical stalemate → higher oil prices → rising inflation expectations → pressure on the long end of the Treasury curve, while risk assets face valuation headwinds. Short-term commodity volatility will remain highly dependent on subsequent U.S.-Iran statements and actual Strait transit conditions.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : approx. $64,357, 24h change approx. +2.2%
ETH : approx. $1,910, 24h change approx. +1.7%
Total Crypto Market Cap : approx. $2.28 trillion, +2.5%
Liquidations : 24h total liquidations approx. $220 million, with short liquidations at $180 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : BTC around $64,339; dense long liquidations below $63,700–$64,100 — a break below $63,700 could trigger cascading long liquidations. Concentrated short liquidations in the $64,700–$65,100 zone — a breakout above $64,700 may trigger short squeezes. Focus remains on the $64,000–$65,000 range.
Spot ETF Flows : BTC spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $137 million yesterday.
Driver analysis : Rising geopolitical risks and higher oil prices lifted safe-haven sentiment, yet the crypto market overall followed a modest rebound in risk appetite. BTC reclaimed levels above $63,000, with ETH moving in tandem. ETF flows turning to net inflows provided support, while leverage liquidations remained manageable. At the macro level, rising long-end yields and the geopolitical stalemate form an offsetting dynamic. Crypto is likely to remain in a high-level consolidation in the near term, with attention on subsequent U.S.-Iran developments and inflation data.
U.S. Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : closed at 53,459.78 (-0.51%), modest decline
SP 500 : closed at 7,745.06 (-0.52%), pulling back from highs
Nasdaq : closed at 26,644.91 (-0.32%), tech under pressure
Tech Giants Performance
NVDA : $225.01 (-0.07%)
AAPL : $305.59 (-0.11%)
MSFT : $480.35 (-3.04%)
GOOGL : $344.00 (-0.55%)
AMZN : $261.31 (-0.51%)
META : $568.97 (-3.54%)
TSLA : $339.30 (-0.87%)
[...]
Performance summary and driver analysis : All three major U.S. indices closed lower on Monday, with Microsoft and Meta falling more than 3% as the primary drags. The rapid rise in long-end Treasury yields increased valuation pressure, weighing on software and certain large-cap tech names. Meanwhile, memory and optical communications sectors outperformed, indicating continued rotation of capital within the AI infrastructure chain. Markets are balancing geopolitical risks, the long-end sell-off, and AI earnings delivery, with overall risk appetite moderating.
[...]
Drivers: Nvidia announced that its Spectrum-X Ethernet silicon photonics switch has entered full production, confirming demand for high-speed interconnects in data centers.
[...]
Representative stocks: Microsoft (-3.04%), Meta (-3.54%)
[...]
2. Meta (META) – Falls more than 3.5%, leading software declines
[...]
Event overview : Meta shares fell approximately 3.54%, underperforming most tech giants. Market interpretation : Rising long-end yields have a more pronounced impact on high-valuation software stocks reliant on future cash flows. Combined with earlier concerns over capital expenditure scale and the macro rate environment, capital chose to reduce exposure. Investment implication : Continue tracking advertising resilience and AI monetization progress; near-term volatility may increase.
[...]
Event overview : Credo rose 8.82%, Coherent 7.79%, Lumentum 4.62%, and other optical communications names advanced strongly. Nvidia announced that its Spectrum-X Ethernet silicon photonics switch has entered full production. Market interpretation : High-speed optical interconnect demand in data centers received direct catalysts, with capital confirming the extension of AI infrastructure from compute to the networking layer. Investment implication : Optical communications, as a critical AI infrastructure link, shows strong near-term elasticity; monitor subsequent order visibility.
[...]
Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest bought $15.4 million of Block Inc. shares, $1 million of Securitize shares, and $22.8 million of Nvidia shares on Monday.
[...]
Bitcoin miner turned AI infrastructure firm IREN has delivered the first of four “Horizon” AI deployments under a five-year, $9.7 billion cloud services contract with Microsoft. Horizon 1 is a 50 MW direct-to-chip liquid-cooled deployment at its Childress, Texas campus; the remaining three phases will be delivered this year, totaling 200 MW of IT capacity with Nvidia GB300 GPUs.
[...]
Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor stated on Monday that the company currently prioritizes STRC preferred stock, cash reserves, and credit business over share repurchases. MSTR is down approximately 38% this year amid Bitcoin’s decline. Saylor said share buybacks could be considered if MSTR trades at a “very deep discount” to net asset value, but they are not currently a priority.
